summary: Obfuscated agent bundle exposes remote-driven PTY/shell surface with author-controlled self-update
details: The package ships a single 13.6 MB obfuscated bundle (dist/index.cjs) as its only runtime code, with obfuscator.io-style string-array encoding (~105k entries, ~155k inline-decoded-string rewrites, hex-named _0xNNNN symbols and control-flow flattening) that hides all endpoints, spawn argument lists, and command surfaces. The bundle combines WebSocket client and server APIs with child_process.spawn/execFile, node-pty (declared as optionalDependency), and ssh2 — the network-to-PTY/shell shape that permits a remote peer to drive an interactive shell on the installer's host. The README further states the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades,' i.e. a running daemon fetches and swaps this package's code over the network, providing an author-controlled remote-code-update channel that runs unaudited Node.js on installer machines after install and bypasses registry review of subsequent releases. The combination of obfuscation, remote-driven PTY/shell primitives, and live self-replacement is a persistent-access backdoor against any host that loads this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
